title: Robinhood Agentic AI
author: Ecstatic-Spread7608
selftext:
I’ve been fascinated by the progress of agentic AI and its potential applications in investing.  
As an experiment, I’ve decided to allocate **$2,500** to an AI-powered investing assistant through Robinhood to see how it performs over time. My goal isn’t to expect instant outperformance, but to better understand how autonomous AI can support investment decisions in real-world market conditions.  
I’m curious to hear from others who have explored this space.  
Have you used agentic AI for investing or trading?  
What platforms or tools have you had success with?  
What lessons or best practices would you recommend?  
I’m looking forward to learning from the experiences of this community and sharing updates on how this experiment unfolds.

comments.author: SnowSilent7695
comments.body:
I had a similar reaction and was intrigued by frontier models' ability to synthesize large datasets in different domains. I am running an experiment, having these models build different strategies, based on historical and real-time data (financials, price and technicals, transcripts, news, etc.) and having them update their strategies based on changing market conditions. I launched at the end of April, and here are the results as of 07/26/2026:

|Strategy|Performance Since Inception|S&P Performance Since Inception|
|:-|:-|:-|
|Value|13.4%|3.3%|
|Momentum|6.6%|3.3%|
|Small/Mid-cap Fundamentals|5.2%|3.3%|
|Blend of Momentum+Fundamentals|\-6.3%|3.3%|

  
Portfolios are rebalanced every week, and I've created a public dashboard that provides more detail on performance and holdings: [https://app.flexreportfinapi.com/stock-picks](https://app.flexreportfinapi.com/stock-picks)

As far as lessons learned from this experiment, data management is by far the most important factor: from cleaning and modeling to ensuring the completeness and timeliness of the data that drives these models' decision-making. Whatever tool you use, I would make sure that this life-cycle is airtight.

comments.author: PloniAlmoni2021
comments.body:
I would say the most important things to worry about are guardrails. If an AI gets something wrong especially if it's running autonomously, things can go really wrong really fast.

If you are interested in how LLMs work with trading, I built a tool to help with investment  exploration (not auto-trading!)
